chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abdullah ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
My father, when he had a need from Allah, would seek it during this time, meaning the decline of the sun (at midday).

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Imam al-Sadiq's father, Imam al-Baqir)

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to make dua according to the practice of the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the time of solar noon (zawal al-shams) as a privileged moment for du'a, aligning with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transition between the Dhuhr and Asr prayers when the veil between the earthly and divine realms is believed to be thinnest. This specific timing is often linked to the concept of 'Istijabah' (acceptance), reflecting the Imams' guidance on optimizing spiritual connection during moments of heightened divine attention.
